distance_segment_segment — 3D geometry op

• Data kinds: primitive → measurement

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.distance_segment_segment(p0, p1, q0, q1) (to call the implementation directly, import match3d; match3d.distance_segment_segment(p0, p1, q0, q1); from the registry, ops3d.get("distance_segment_segment"))

• Return value through the ledger: fullseye.ledger.distance_segment_segment(...) returns only the declared out type measurement (the underlying function also returns auxiliary values). When you need what was dropped, use fullseye.ledger.distance_segment_segment.raw(...) or call match3d.distance_segment_segment directly.

Usage

Shortest distance between finite line segments and the pair of their closest points. → (distance, cp, cq).

distance_line_line is the distance between infinite lines, so it can return 0 for 2 segments that are apart (measured: 0.0 for (0,0,0)-(1,0,0) and (5,0,0)-(6,0,0), ground truth 4.0). Limbs, robot links, pipes and tools are all finite, so for safety distances or interference checks the infinite-line version underestimates the danger (in the poc_safety_clearance measurement, an 87.6 % underestimate for the same 2 segments).

Args:

p0, p1: endpoints of segment 1, (3,). If p0 == p1 it is treated as a point.

q0, q1: endpoints of segment 2, (3,).

Returns:

(distance, cp, cq): the shortest distance as float, and the closest points on the segment-1 side and the segment-2 side,

(3,). distance == 0 when the 2 segments intersect (or touch).

★Via the ledger (fullseye.ledger.distance_segment_segment) only the declared out type

distance is returned. When you also need the closest points, use

fullseye.ledger.distance_segment_segment.raw(...).

Raises:

ValueError: when an endpoint cannot be converted to (3,), or is non-finite.

Parallel and degenerate cases (segments collapsed to a point) are also handled correctly by branching (Ericson, *Real-Time Collision Detection*, §5.1.9, clamped closest-point method). The distance between capsules (core line + radius) is distance - r1 - r2; interference means that it becomes negative.

Reference (public): C. Ericson, *Real-Time Collision Detection*, Morgan Kaufmann 2005, §5.1.9 "Closest Points of Two Line Segments".
